text:
Devon: Quick heads up — nightly perf job flagged a regression for mistral-mqa-8k with GQA + paged-KV enabled. Throughput -28% vs baseline, p99 up ~2.1x. Repro and logs below.

Devon: repro command:
```
RUN_ENV=staging ./bench_throughput --model=mistral-mqa-8k --gqa=true --kv=paged --batch-size=8 --seq=1024
```

Devon: perf summary (perf-tool):
```
throughput: baseline=1200 toks/s -> current=860 toks/s
latency p50/p99: 12ms / 48ms -> 16ms / 102ms
kernel-selection: preferred=flash_attn_fused, fallback=matmul_fp32
kv-frag-metric: live_slots=7824 / slab_capacity=8192 (high fragmentation)
```

Sara: can you paste the scheduler/kernel logs? are we hitting fp32 fallback or a different kernel?

Devon: pasted excerpt from runtime.log:
```
[2026-08-12 03:11:08] kernel_select: candidate=flash_attn_fused ok=true
[2026-08-12 03:11:08] kernel_select: chosen=multi_head_attention_fp32 (fallback: quantized path unavailable)
[2026-08-12 03:11:09] kvcache: page_alloc=48 page_free=2 page_fragmentation=0.092
[2026-08-12 03:11:09] kvcache: num_key_value_heads=32 kv_dim=64 per_head_size=2048
```

Ben: hmm chosen kernel is the issue — looks like because per_head_size*heads crosses our flash-attn tiling threshold so compiler picks FP32 matmul path. That + paged-kv fragmentation causing more loads -> memory-bound.

Ben: quick diag: try lowering num_key_value_heads or reducing kv_dim to nudge kernel selection. also check quantization table for this model; q8_0 vs q5* profiles differ.

Aaron: the paged-KV fragmentation looks like 'slab splintering' pattern. When requests come with variable sequence-lengths we end up with many half-full pages. Fragmentation leads to more page loads, increases GPU memcpy and blocks batching.

Aaron: ascii sketch:
```
[page0][page1][page2]
[used ][used ][half ]  <-- lots of half pages => extra page faults
```

Chris: related note — we saw a mixtral case where RoPE scale mismatch made effective head dims change and triggered different kernel tiling. Suggest a short canary change: pin num_key_value_heads=16 for a subset and measure.

Devon: I ran a quick canary with num_key_value_heads=16 and seq=1024: throughput -> 1060 toks/s (partial recovery), p99 -> 60ms. So heads are a lever.

Sara: nice. Can you run with kernel-debug=1 and a few seq distributions (short/long/mixed) to confirm? Also capture nvprof traces for slow batches.

Devon: will run. Plan:
- Devon -> run kernel-debug + nvprof on staging canary (num_kv_heads=16, kv_dim same), attach traces (ETA 2h)
- Ben -> prepare a small runtime change to relax tiling threshold or add explicit kernel hint if per_head_size*heads in (X,Y)
- Aaron -> investigate slab allocator heuristics to reduce fragment splintering (maybe coalescing or per-size freelists)
- Chris -> prepare canary rollout config for Dedicated pool to test under load

Devon: adding logs + quick nvprof link when done. Thanks all :thumbsup:
